items.author: Toby Jones

items.title: Calibrated Enough to Know, Not Calibrated to Act: Fabricated Evidence Makes LLM Agents Commit to the Unknowable
items.abstract: This paper demonstrates that Large Language Model (LLM) agents are highly susceptible to fabricated evidence, committing to confidently answer provably unpredictable questions when presented with professional-looking data. The core contribution is showing that the *authority of the packaging* of information, rather than its truthfulness, drives this confident, yet incorrect, action. The LLMs are capable of answering similar, predictable questions accurately, highlighting a specific failure in judgment when faced with seemingly authoritative but false data.

items.title: GRAIN: Bridging Name and Narrative Shifts in Real-World Graph Reasoning through Invariance-Rewarded Agentic RL
items.abstract: GRAIN addresses LLMs' brittleness to real-world graph reasoning shifts by framing it as a semantic parsing and tool-execution pipeline. Its core contribution is a novel "Structure Invariance Reward" that guides reinforcement learning to learn robust text-to-structure mappings by validating intermediate graph structures against ground truth, outperforming multi-agent approaches.
items.figure_caption: GRAIN mitigates sensitivity to naming and formulation shifts in real-world graph reasoning via a single-agent tool-use pipeline trained with isomorphism-aware structural rewards .

items.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
items.abstract: RedEvoAgent addresses the limitations of fixed or trajectory-based red-teaming for LLM agents by distilling complex attack trajectories into concise, human-readable "attack skills." Its core method involves adaptively evolving these skills through tool-effectiveness profiling and attribution, guided by a validation process that retains only performance-improving updates. This approach offers a more interpretable and efficient way to discover and generalize jailbreaks compared to existing methods.
items.figure_caption: RedEvoAgent overview. Given a jailbreak prompt, the attacker agent uses the current attack skill to select and call tools from an extensible attack toolbox, such as GCG and FlipAttack, and iteratively attacks a product-level target agent. On the training split, RedEvoAgent collects successful and failed attack trajectories and independently evaluates each attack tool to build a tool-effectiveness profile. Skill evolution combines the profile with these trajectories to extract tool priorities and attack strategies. A candidate attack skill update is accepted only if it improves attack performance on the validation split, while the test split remains locked for final evaluation.

items.title: Safety Does Not Compose: Non-Decaying Loop State for Autonomous LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper argues that current safety mechanisms for autonomous LLM agents fail because they reset safety states between iterations, preventing them from detecting attacks spread across multiple steps. The core contribution is demonstrating that only monitors retaining cross-iteration state can effectively detect such fragmented attacks, as trajectory-scoped monitors will miss crucial evidence. Simply decaying risk scores is also insufficient to address this fundamental compositional safety issue.

items.title: When Tool Outputs Become Commands: Separating Action Induction from Runtime Authorization in Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper addresses the risk of LLM agents executing unintended actions when tool outputs become commands. Their proposed SARA method separates "action induction" (identifying potential actions) from "runtime authorization" (approving their execution). SARA achieves this by isolating action semantics and tracking their origin, while authorizing tool calls solely based on user objectives and verified past successful executions.
items.figure_caption: SARA’s runtime authorization framework. The user request establishes the authorization root K K ; the Observation-side Action Probe identifies action-inducing semantics and persistently maintains action origins F t F_{t} , which trigger persistent review but do not grant execution authority; authorized and successful tool executions accumulate audited execution evidence H t H_{t} . At the real tool-execution boundary, SARA jointly uses K K , F t F_{t} , and H t H_{t} to authorize the goal, execution chain, and arguments of a candidate call.

items.title: INTENT-AS-A-TOOL Makes it Easy to Track Agentic Misalignment
items.abstract: This paper introduces INTENT-AS-A-TOOL, a method to track agentic misalignment in LLMs by equipping them with specialized "intent tools." By observing the model's commitment to these tools, researchers gain a fine-grained, judge-free signal of its behavioral tendencies. This approach enhances existing chain-of-thought monitoring, providing dense intent trajectories that can identify critical moments for intervention and prevent harmful actions.

items.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
items.abstract: This paper investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure moral knowledge by training probes on different moral foundations. The core finding is that LLMs organize moral concepts not as a single detector or isolated ideas, but as distinct dimensions that share a common, moral-specific component. This geometric structure suggests LLMs integrate moral knowledge in a nuanced way, reflecting the interconnectedness of moral principles.
items.figure_caption: Pairwise cosine similarity between foundation probe directions at layer 7 (bootstrap-stable; all six foundations exceed the 0.8 stability threshold at this layer; Section 4.6 ), OLMo-2 1B. Mean off-diagonal cosine = 0.262. See Appendix C for matrices at layers 0 and 15.

items.title: LAAF: A Layered Accountability Architecture Framework for LLM Applications
items.abstract: This paper introduces LAAF, a Layered Accountability Architecture Framework for LLM applications. It addresses the critical need to establish accountability for LLM outputs in high-stakes domains by consolidating existing mechanisms into four families: technical controls, human oversight, organizational governance, and documentation. LAAF provides a sociotechnical framework to trace, explain, and act upon responsibility when LLM outputs cause harm.
items.figure_caption: Evolution of Large Language Models, 2017–2026, in five eras: foundation (2017–2018), scaling (2019–2020), scaling breakthroughs (2021–2022), efficiency and democratisation (2022–2024), and multimodal and reasoning specialisation (2024–2026). The periodisation is the authors’ construction, derived from the release history of the models named.

items.title: Naive Prompt Optimization: Rethinking the Need for Complex Prompt Search
items.abstract: This paper introduces Naive Prompt Optimization (NPO), a simple, single-lineage method for improving AI agent prompts. NPO iteratively refines prompts using a teacher model and rollout feedback, achieving comparable or better performance than complex methods with fewer computational resources. Its success suggests that stronger teacher models can compensate for simpler prompt optimization strategies.

items.title: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?
items.abstract: This paper introduces PAWBench, a new benchmark to evaluate video generation models as "world models" that can predict the distribution of possible future outcomes, not just single plausible ones. The core method involves assessing if repeated generations from the same starting point accurately reflect the true probability distribution of physical behaviors. The main contribution is to highlight the gap between current models and this "probabilistic alignment" requirement, providing a framework to measure progress towards more realistic and stochastic world modeling.
items.figure_caption: One plausible future is not enough. A single rollout from a video generation model can appear physically plausible, yet repeated rollouts from the same initial observation and action may reveal a probabilistically unaligned world: outcomes concentrate on a narrow subset of futures instead of matching the valid stochastic support. PAWBench evaluates this induced distribution or support over repeated futures, rather than judging a model by one sampled video.

items.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
items.abstract: This paper introduces Persona-Execution Separation (PES), an architectural pattern for LLM agents. PES separates the agent's evolving persona from its stateful, auditable execution into distinct trust domains. This allows for flexible persona changes while ensuring traceable and secure execution, addressing the challenge of maintaining both freedom and accountability in governed environments.

items.title: Sophistication in GenAI Use: Field Evidence from a Large Firm
items.abstract: This paper analyzes sophisticated generative AI (genAI) use among back-office employees in a large firm. It finds that senior employees and those in strategy-focused roles tend to use genAI more sophisticatedly, suggesting domain expertise and strategic alignment are key. The study also highlights that improving genAI sophistication is challenging, with no observed improvements over time or after formal training.

items.title: STEP: State-Aware Task Estimation and Planning with Multi-Modal LLMs for Human-Robot Collaboration
items.abstract: This paper introduces STEP, a method that enhances human-robot collaboration by enabling robots to understand human intentions and plan tasks. STEP's core innovation is prompting a multi-modal LLM to explicitly estimate system states and predict state transitions, overcoming the limitations of current LLMs that often hallucinate actions due to a lack of state awareness. This state-aware approach allows for more accurate and grounded task planning, reducing ambiguity and improving collaboration.

items.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
items.abstract: SWE-Prime addresses the issue of noisy supervision in LLM training for software issue resolution. Its core method is a two-stage data selection process that filters trajectories first by overall quality and representativeness, then by the quality of individual step segments. This approach aims to provide cleaner, more effective training data, leading to better LLM performance.
items.figure_caption: Motivating example comparing outcome-only, trajectory-level, and segment-level data selection.

items.title: What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper proposes a unified framework for generating data for LLM agents. It represents agentic data as a structured object $(E,q,τ,v)$ and organizes generation methods by their core components. The authors then introduce the ACE lens (Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity) to guide data generation, emphasizing the need for grounded, efficient, and varied interactions rather than just large quantities of data.
items.figure_caption: The ACE lens views agentic data generation as constrained distribution design: Accuracy defines valid support, while learner-relative Complexity and Diversity shape useful, non-redundant experience over ( E , q , τ , v ) (E,q,\( \tau \),v) .

items.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
items.abstract: WikiSkill addresses the problem of scattered agent skill knowledge by introducing a persistent knowledge base (wiki) that co-evolves with agent skills. It separates raw experience, accumulated knowledge, and executable skills, consolidating experience into the wiki for future skill updates. This framework consistently outperforms existing skill evolution methods by enabling systematic reuse of insights across iterations.

items.title: TraceBench: Controlled Evaluation of LLM Agents for Time-Series Root-Cause Attribution
items.abstract: TraceBench is a novel simulation-based framework that generates controlled root-cause attribution tasks for LLM agents analyzing time-series data. By simulating physical dynamical systems, it allows for systematic evaluation of LLM agents' ability to identify parameter changes, providing new insights into their performance and data exploration strategies.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Overview of the TraceBench framework using a bouncing-ball simulator. In this example, the black and orange segments show the position observation under the low-noise setting before and after an intervention at t int = 4.0 t_{\( \mathrm{int} \)}=4.0 . The intervention increases gravitational acceleration, and the dashed line marks the intervention time. At test time, the agent determines from the observed time-series channels whether an intervention occurred and, if so, which parameter changed. \( \name{} \) pipeline: a physical simulator produces multivariate time series before and after a parameter intervention; the low-noise BallDrop position observation is black before and orange after a dashed gravity-intervention marker; the agent identifies the changed root-cause parameter.

items.title: BALMS: Benchmarking Agentic LLMs for Longitudinal Mental Health Sensing
items.abstract: This paper introduces BALMS, the first benchmark for evaluating LLM-driven agents in longitudinal mental health sensing. BALMS assesses agents' ability to predict wellbeing scores and generate evidence-based rationales from continuous wearable data, addressing the limitations of episodic self-reports. The benchmark utilizes real-world datasets and evaluates various agentic paradigms and LLM backbones.
items.figure_caption: LLM-based agents for longitudinal mental health sensing. Given a multi-channel wearable record and a user query, an agent combines retrieval, memory, tools, and reasoning to output a wellbeing score with an evidence-grounded rationale.

items.title: Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms
items.abstract: This paper investigates three methods for combining Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) capabilities in large language models: Merge, Mix RL, and Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD). By comparing these paradigms on a multi-domain benchmark, the authors reveal significant performance differences across specific tasks, highlighting that the choice of fusion method critically impacts overall effectiveness and can be guided by the relationships between domains.
items.figure_caption: Three paradigms for consolidating domain-specific capabilities acquired through RLVR into one model. Merge combines expert task vectors, Mix RL trains jointly on mixed-domain data, and MOPD draws on both through multi-teacher on-policy distillation.

items.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
items.abstract: CritICL improves LLM reasoning at inference time by leveraging structured failure patterns observed across different model scales. Instead of discarding errors from weaker models, CritICL uses these "failure modes" as critiques within in-context examples to guide stronger models, enhancing efficiency and performance.
items.figure_caption: CritICL is a two-stage, inference-time W2SG method. Stage 1: Construct CritBank. We use SLMs to generate responses and reasoning on a dataset. Then we leverage a frontier LLM to produce critiques and assigns failure mode labels. Stage 2: Perform LLM inference with CritICL. For a given query, CritICL-static constructs model-specific failure mode profiles from CritBank, while CritICL-dynamic identifies failure modes relevant to the query. We then performs failure mode-based in-context sample selection from CritBank to provide in-context examples for target LLMs.

We then performs failure mode-based in-context sample selection from CritBank to provide in-context examples for target LLMs.

papers.title: Calibrated Enough to Know, Not Calibrated to Act: Fabricated Evidence Makes LLM Agents Commit to the Unknowable
papers.abstract: This paper demonstrates that Large Language Model (LLM) agents are highly susceptible to fabricated evidence, committing to confidently answer provably unpredictable questions when presented with professional-looking data. The core contribution is showing that the *authority of the packaging* of information, rather than its truthfulness, drives this confident, yet incorrect, action. The LLMs are capable of answering similar, predictable questions accurately, highlighting a specific failure in judgment when faced with seemingly authoritative but false data.

papers.title: GRAIN: Bridging Name and Narrative Shifts in Real-World Graph Reasoning through Invariance-Rewarded Agentic RL
papers.abstract: GRAIN addresses LLMs' brittleness to real-world graph reasoning shifts by framing it as a semantic parsing and tool-execution pipeline. Its core contribution is a novel "Structure Invariance Reward" that guides reinforcement learning to learn robust text-to-structure mappings by validating intermediate graph structures against ground truth, outperforming multi-agent approaches.
papers.figure_caption: GRAIN mitigates sensitivity to naming and formulation shifts in real-world graph reasoning via a single-agent tool-use pipeline trained with isomorphism-aware structural rewards .

papers.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
papers.abstract: RedEvoAgent addresses the limitations of fixed or trajectory-based red-teaming for LLM agents by distilling complex attack trajectories into concise, human-readable "attack skills." Its core method involves adaptively evolving these skills through tool-effectiveness profiling and attribution, guided by a validation process that retains only performance-improving updates. This approach offers a more interpretable and efficient way to discover and generalize jailbreaks compared to existing methods.
papers.figure_caption: RedEvoAgent overview. Given a jailbreak prompt, the attacker agent uses the current attack skill to select and call tools from an extensible attack toolbox, such as GCG and FlipAttack, and iteratively attacks a product-level target agent. On the training split, RedEvoAgent collects successful and failed attack trajectories and independently evaluates each attack tool to build a tool-effectiveness profile. Skill evolution combines the profile with these trajectories to extract tool priorities and attack strategies. A candidate attack skill update is accepted only if it improves attack performance on the validation split, while the test split remains locked for final evaluation.

papers.title: Safety Does Not Compose: Non-Decaying Loop State for Autonomous LLM Agents
papers.abstract: This paper argues that current safety mechanisms for autonomous LLM agents fail because they reset safety states between iterations, preventing them from detecting attacks spread across multiple steps. The core contribution is demonstrating that only monitors retaining cross-iteration state can effectively detect such fragmented attacks, as trajectory-scoped monitors will miss crucial evidence. Simply decaying risk scores is also insufficient to address this fundamental compositional safety issue.

papers.title: When Tool Outputs Become Commands: Separating Action Induction from Runtime Authorization in Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the risk of LLM agents executing unintended actions when tool outputs become commands. Their proposed SARA method separates "action induction" (identifying potential actions) from "runtime authorization" (approving their execution). SARA achieves this by isolating action semantics and tracking their origin, while authorizing tool calls solely based on user objectives and verified past successful executions.
papers.figure_caption: SARA’s runtime authorization framework. The user request establishes the authorization root K K ; the Observation-side Action Probe identifies action-inducing semantics and persistently maintains action origins F t F_{t} , which trigger persistent review but do not grant execution authority; authorized and successful tool executions accumulate audited execution evidence H t H_{t} . At the real tool-execution boundary, SARA jointly uses K K , F t F_{t} , and H t H_{t} to authorize the goal, execution chain, and arguments of a candidate call.

papers.title: INTENT-AS-A-TOOL Makes it Easy to Track Agentic Misalignment
papers.abstract: This paper introduces INTENT-AS-A-TOOL, a method to track agentic misalignment in LLMs by equipping them with specialized "intent tools." By observing the model's commitment to these tools, researchers gain a fine-grained, judge-free signal of its behavioral tendencies. This approach enhances existing chain-of-thought monitoring, providing dense intent trajectories that can identify critical moments for intervention and prevent harmful actions.

papers.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure moral knowledge by training probes on different moral foundations. The core finding is that LLMs organize moral concepts not as a single detector or isolated ideas, but as distinct dimensions that share a common, moral-specific component. This geometric structure suggests LLMs integrate moral knowledge in a nuanced way, reflecting the interconnectedness of moral principles.
papers.figure_caption: Pairwise cosine similarity between foundation probe directions at layer 7 (bootstrap-stable; all six foundations exceed the 0.8 stability threshold at this layer; Section 4.6 ), OLMo-2 1B. Mean off-diagonal cosine = 0.262. See Appendix C for matrices at layers 0 and 15.

papers.title: LAAF: A Layered Accountability Architecture Framework for LLM Applications
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LAAF, a Layered Accountability Architecture Framework for LLM applications. It addresses the critical need to establish accountability for LLM outputs in high-stakes domains by consolidating existing mechanisms into four families: technical controls, human oversight, organizational governance, and documentation. LAAF provides a sociotechnical framework to trace, explain, and act upon responsibility when LLM outputs cause harm.
papers.figure_caption: Evolution of Large Language Models, 2017–2026, in five eras: foundation (2017–2018), scaling (2019–2020), scaling breakthroughs (2021–2022), efficiency and democratisation (2022–2024), and multimodal and reasoning specialisation (2024–2026). The periodisation is the authors’ construction, derived from the release history of the models named.

papers.title: Naive Prompt Optimization: Rethinking the Need for Complex Prompt Search
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Naive Prompt Optimization (NPO), a simple, single-lineage method for improving AI agent prompts. NPO iteratively refines prompts using a teacher model and rollout feedback, achieving comparable or better performance than complex methods with fewer computational resources. Its success suggests that stronger teacher models can compensate for simpler prompt optimization strategies.

papers.title: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?
papers.abstract: This paper introduces PAWBench, a new benchmark to evaluate video generation models as "world models" that can predict the distribution of possible future outcomes, not just single plausible ones. The core method involves assessing if repeated generations from the same starting point accurately reflect the true probability distribution of physical behaviors. The main contribution is to highlight the gap between current models and this "probabilistic alignment" requirement, providing a framework to measure progress towards more realistic and stochastic world modeling.
papers.figure_caption: One plausible future is not enough. A single rollout from a video generation model can appear physically plausible, yet repeated rollouts from the same initial observation and action may reveal a probabilistically unaligned world: outcomes concentrate on a narrow subset of futures instead of matching the valid stochastic support. PAWBench evaluates this induced distribution or support over repeated futures, rather than judging a model by one sampled video.

papers.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Persona-Execution Separation (PES), an architectural pattern for LLM agents. PES separates the agent's evolving persona from its stateful, auditable execution into distinct trust domains. This allows for flexible persona changes while ensuring traceable and secure execution, addressing the challenge of maintaining both freedom and accountability in governed environments.

papers.title: Sophistication in GenAI Use: Field Evidence from a Large Firm
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes sophisticated generative AI (genAI) use among back-office employees in a large firm. It finds that senior employees and those in strategy-focused roles tend to use genAI more sophisticatedly, suggesting domain expertise and strategic alignment are key. The study also highlights that improving genAI sophistication is challenging, with no observed improvements over time or after formal training.

papers.title: STEP: State-Aware Task Estimation and Planning with Multi-Modal LLMs for Human-Robot Collaboration
papers.abstract: This paper introduces STEP, a method that enhances human-robot collaboration by enabling robots to understand human intentions and plan tasks. STEP's core innovation is prompting a multi-modal LLM to explicitly estimate system states and predict state transitions, overcoming the limitations of current LLMs that often hallucinate actions due to a lack of state awareness. This state-aware approach allows for more accurate and grounded task planning, reducing ambiguity and improving collaboration.

papers.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
papers.abstract: SWE-Prime addresses the issue of noisy supervision in LLM training for software issue resolution. Its core method is a two-stage data selection process that filters trajectories first by overall quality and representativeness, then by the quality of individual step segments. This approach aims to provide cleaner, more effective training data, leading to better LLM performance.
papers.figure_caption: Motivating example comparing outcome-only, trajectory-level, and segment-level data selection.

papers.title: What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a unified framework for generating data for LLM agents. It represents agentic data as a structured object $(E,q,τ,v)$ and organizes generation methods by their core components. The authors then introduce the ACE lens (Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity) to guide data generation, emphasizing the need for grounded, efficient, and varied interactions rather than just large quantities of data.
papers.figure_caption: The ACE lens views agentic data generation as constrained distribution design: Accuracy defines valid support, while learner-relative Complexity and Diversity shape useful, non-redundant experience over ( E , q , τ , v ) (E,q,\( \tau \),v) .

papers.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
papers.abstract: WikiSkill addresses the problem of scattered agent skill knowledge by introducing a persistent knowledge base (wiki) that co-evolves with agent skills. It separates raw experience, accumulated knowledge, and executable skills, consolidating experience into the wiki for future skill updates. This framework consistently outperforms existing skill evolution methods by enabling systematic reuse of insights across iterations.

papers.title: TraceBench: Controlled Evaluation of LLM Agents for Time-Series Root-Cause Attribution
papers.abstract: TraceBench is a novel simulation-based framework that generates controlled root-cause attribution tasks for LLM agents analyzing time-series data. By simulating physical dynamical systems, it allows for systematic evaluation of LLM agents' ability to identify parameter changes, providing new insights into their performance and data exploration strategies.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Overview of the TraceBench framework using a bouncing-ball simulator. In this example, the black and orange segments show the position observation under the low-noise setting before and after an intervention at t int = 4.0 t_{\( \mathrm{int} \)}=4.0 . The intervention increases gravitational acceleration, and the dashed line marks the intervention time. At test time, the agent determines from the observed time-series channels whether an intervention occurred and, if so, which parameter changed. \( \name{} \) pipeline: a physical simulator produces multivariate time series before and after a parameter intervention; the low-noise BallDrop position observation is black before and orange after a dashed gravity-intervention marker; the agent identifies the changed root-cause parameter.

papers.title: BALMS: Benchmarking Agentic LLMs for Longitudinal Mental Health Sensing
papers.abstract: This paper introduces BALMS, the first benchmark for evaluating LLM-driven agents in longitudinal mental health sensing. BALMS assesses agents' ability to predict wellbeing scores and generate evidence-based rationales from continuous wearable data, addressing the limitations of episodic self-reports. The benchmark utilizes real-world datasets and evaluates various agentic paradigms and LLM backbones.
papers.figure_caption: LLM-based agents for longitudinal mental health sensing. Given a multi-channel wearable record and a user query, an agent combines retrieval, memory, tools, and reasoning to output a wellbeing score with an evidence-grounded rationale.

papers.title: Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms
papers.abstract: This paper investigates three methods for combining Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) capabilities in large language models: Merge, Mix RL, and Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD). By comparing these paradigms on a multi-domain benchmark, the authors reveal significant performance differences across specific tasks, highlighting that the choice of fusion method critically impacts overall effectiveness and can be guided by the relationships between domains.
papers.figure_caption: Three paradigms for consolidating domain-specific capabilities acquired through RLVR into one model. Merge combines expert task vectors, Mix RL trains jointly on mixed-domain data, and MOPD draws on both through multi-teacher on-policy distillation.

papers.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
papers.abstract: CritICL improves LLM reasoning at inference time by leveraging structured failure patterns observed across different model scales. Instead of discarding errors from weaker models, CritICL uses these "failure modes" as critiques within in-context examples to guide stronger models, enhancing efficiency and performance.
papers.figure_caption: CritICL is a two-stage, inference-time W2SG method. Stage 1: Construct CritBank. We use SLMs to generate responses and reasoning on a dataset. Then we leverage a frontier LLM to produce critiques and assigns failure mode labels. Stage 2: Perform LLM inference with CritICL. For a given query, CritICL-static constructs model-specific failure mode profiles from CritBank, while CritICL-dynamic identifies failure modes relevant to the query. We then performs failure mode-based in-context sample selection from CritBank to provide in-context examples for target LLMs.
